content.title: Under Armour (UAA) Q2 Earnings: Taking a Look at Key Metrics Versus Estimates
content.summary: While the top- and bottom-line numbers for Under Armour (UAA) give a sense of how the business performed in the quarter ended September 2025, it could be worth looking at how some of its key metrics compare to Wall Street estimates and year-ago values.

content.title: Under Armour Swings to Quarterly Loss, Expects Lower FY26 Revenue
content.summary: Under Armour swung to a fiscal second-quarter loss as sales of sportswear fell, a trend it warned is likely to continue during the balance of its fiscal year.

content.title: Under Armour’s (NYSE:UAA) Q3 Sales Top Estimates
content.summary: Athletic apparel company Under Armour (NYSE:UAA) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q3 CY2025, but sales fell by 4.7% year on year to $1.33 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.04 per share was $0.02 above analysts’ consensus estimates.

content.title: Under Armour (UAA) Beats Q2 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
content.summary: Under Armour (UAA) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of +33.33% and +1.98%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 2025. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?

content.title: Under Armour Beats Q2 EPS and Sales Projections, but Lowers Full-year Forecast
content.summary: The Baltimore-based sports brand is in the midst of a restructuring plan.

content.title: Under Armour beats fiscal Q2 forecasts, misses on profit outlook; new CFO unveiled
content.summary: Investing.com -- Under Armour reported results for the second quarter of fiscal 2026 that were just above analyst estimates, while its full-year earnings outlook fell short of consensus.

content.title: Under Armour: Fiscal Q2 Earnings Snapshot
content.summary: The Baltimore-based company said it had a loss of 4 cents per share. Earnings, adjusted for one-time gains and costs, came to 4 cents per share. The results surpassed Wall Street expectations.

content.title: Under Armour CFO to exit next year
content.summary: Dave Bergman has spent 21 years with the retailer, nine of them as its financial chief, and will be replaced by Samsonite executive Reza Taleghani.
